about: What the scene and the movement code may rely on in the shipped models. packages/office-assets builds them and its check (bun run models:check, and its contract test in CI) verifies every built file against this; the build fails if one doesn't match. Changing anything here is a breaking or additive change for the product: bump contractVersion (major = removed/renamed, minor = added, patch = notes only).

changelog.5.0.1: Notes only: the models are now generated in 3d-office's packages/office-assets (agent-office is retired), so the notes point there and at office-sim instead of agent-office's viewer and tools.
changelog.5.0.0: Breaking: the framed print in the pod area is gone, and with it node static-art, material art and scene extras artAtlas. Night lights renamed to the areas they light now: reading -> meeting-room, kitchen -> maintenance-bar, lounge -> concourse. Added: the agent board is live: its own node agent-board + material agent_board (draw rows into its emissive map; scene extras agentBoard gives size and pixels). robot.glb / robot-lite.glb: tool-icon joints icon_terminal, icon_search, icon_edit, icon_web on the head, resting at scale 0; the product scales the current tool's joint to 1 (no clip drives them). New file minibot.glb: a sub-agent that trails its parent agent (clips Hover, Fly, Work, Pop_In, Pop_Out; reference logic Minibot in viewer/agent-sim.js). The lobby queue spots are gone: POI kind queue removed; queued agents wait on poi-stand-entry-<queue position> (assign "position"), the lobby's standing spots, 1 = nearest the door.
changelog.4.6.0: Queueing. The office seats agents.max agents (pod N, docking bay N, status light N = slot N). Sessions beyond that are queued: new agent state queued (yellow) waits at new POI kind queue 1..6 in the lobby (poi-queue-1 is the front, spots face into the office), then stand-entry overflow spots. Slot assign "position" = poi-<kind>-<queue position>. Reference logic: Roster in viewer/agent-sim.js (sessions -> slots 1..max, FIFO queue, the queue head takes a freed slot) and Agent.setDesk (re-target as the queue moves up).
changelog.4.5.0: Desks are work pods: one continuous console per row, curved screen, cockpit seat with a data umbilical, frosted wings, station plate 01-10, and a status_glow ring on the floor round each seat (desk N's ring samples texel N-1 like its strip, so the product needs no change). New material frosted (transparent, in static-glass). The lobby by the door: hang-out seat rows (sit_idle 7-8 moved there), wayfinding totem, showcase, agent board (screens atlas entry departures); a painted concourse from the door to the dock. POI names, kinds and ids unchanged.
changelog.4.4.0: Layout and behaviour. Room is x -11..10 (21 x 14 m); the docking bay (zone server_room, x -11..-6.5) is 1 m narrower. Zone rects changed: workspace x -6.5..3, z -7..0.6 (meeting room + desks), lounge x -6.5..3, z 0.6..2.5 (open floor above the factory, launch pad), entry x 3..10 (north-east corner + the door). State done now dances in place on the production line: slots poi-ship-* then poi-stand-deploy-*, clip Dance (was Celebrate on the pad by the door). Desks 1-10 now sit in 2 rows of 5 facing west toward the dock (sit_work POIs face -x; desks 1-5 are the west row). sit_idle 1, 2, 5, 6 are in a glass meeting room (north-west), 3-4 training pods moved to the north-east corner. The CHARGING DOCK portal is gone. POI names, kinds and ids are unchanged; read positions from the POI nodes.
changelog.4.3.0: The middle of the office is now factory support. POI names, kinds and ids are unchanged; positions and what they look like changed: sit_idle 1, 2, 5, 6 are operator seats at the control-room console (lounge zone, robots face the video wall, away from the camera), 3-4 training pods (reading nook -> training bay), 7-8 the arrivals bench by the door (facing the camera); use_coffee is the maintenance bar's coolant dispenser, coffee_chat 1-3 stand round the service counter. anim-steam-N is now coolant vapour at the dispenser. Visual: archive cabinets, training-progress wall screen, hydroponic grow rack, ARRIVALS scanner gate inside the door, floor stencil CONTROL ROOM.
changelog.4.2.1: anim-core is gone (the data core centrepiece was removed; the contract never required it by name, the product only plays the Ambient clip). Floor stencil DOCKING BAY across the middle of the dock.
changelog.4.2.0: Additive (no renames or removals). The server room is now the data core / charging dock and the room is 2 m wider: x -12..10 (22 x 14 m), zone server_room is x -12..-6.5; charging bays moved west with it (POI names, kinds and ids unchanged; positions changed, read them from the POI nodes as always). New anim-* nodes in the Ambient clip: anim-core (the data core's inner pods, a quarter turn per loop), anim-shuttle-1 and anim-shuttle-2 (rack-top shuttles), anim-link (data capsules in the glass tube from the flash station to the fabricator). Visual: docking cradles, glass-door racks with bay plates 01-10, cable tray + coolant pipes, the data core centrepiece, a CHARGING DOCK portal over the opening, floor paint. Smaller round parts are tessellated by size (about 9k fewer triangles elsewhere); office budget raised to 80k triangles / 760 KB for the new room.
changelog.4.1.0: Additive (no renames or removals). The deploy line is now an agent factory: new anim-* nodes anim-arm-1 and anim-arm-2 (two robot arms whose turrets swing in the Ambient clip); the conveyor carries freshly built, unpainted robots instead of gadgets and crates (still node anim-conveyor). Visual only: one pale lab floor (raised-access panels) across the whole office, perforated in the server room; steel guard rails replace the planters between the lounge and the factory; a gantry with station plates 01-08 runs behind the workbenches (its LED bar uses lamp_glow, so it follows the day/night rule like the other lamps); painted floor markings. POIs, states, zones, materials and night lights are unchanged.
changelog.4.0.0: Colour means status. Office re-planned around three jobs: charging bays (server room, west, unchanged), desks (north) and a deploy line (south) where robots hammer and tinker at workbenches while gadgets ride the belt to dispatch; a lounge, reading nook, kitchenette and waiting area hold idle agents. Zones are now server_room, workspace, lounge, entry, deploy. Agent states are working, shipping, waiting_for_input, idle, paused_or_rate_limited, error, done, arrive (removed: planning, designing, researching, testing, meeting); each has a color (green / yellow / orange / red, see statusColors) for the robot's primary material and its desk / bay light. Owner colours are gone: owner_glow + owner_fabric + owner_colors -> status_glow + status_colors (scene extras statusColors; chairs are a neutral fabric). waiting_for_input now waits at the agent's own desk; done celebrates on the pad by the door (moved to the middle of the east wall). POI kinds removed: sit_meet, present, plan_lead, plan, sit_design, design, sit_research, browse, test, sit_test, play; sit_idle is now 1..8 (sofa, armchairs), coffee_chat 1..3 (bar table), ship 1..8 (workbenches). New material art (framed prints, scene extras artAtlas) in node static-art. Ambient clip: server LEDs no longer blink, the test-rig turntable is gone; coffee steam (kitchen) and conveyor cargo remain. Robot: joint hammer (hidden at rest) and clips Hammer, Tinker; primary is neutral grey by default (the product colours it by status). Budgets raised: office 74k triangles / 720 KB for the decor, robot 15.5k triangles for the hammer.
changelog.3.0.0: Office re-planned as a 20 x 14 m 'data centre' office. Zones are now server_room, boardroom, design, planning, testlab, lounge, library, workspace, shipping (removed: canteen, hub, breakout). Charging moved to the server room: one bay per agent (charge 1..agents.max, bay N in owner colour N via owner_glow) and paused_or_rate_limited sends each agent to its own bay (assign 'own' now works for any kind numbered 1..agents.max). New agent states planning, designing, researching, testing, shipping, with new POI kinds plan_lead, plan, sit_design, design, sit_research, browse, test, sit_test, ship. done now celebrates on the shipping bay's launch pad. sit_meet 1..8; sit_idle 1-2 sofa, 3-4 bean bags (cafe seats removed); use_coffee is at the coffee bar. Night lights renamed per zone. anim-* adds anim-turntable and anim-conveyor. Budgets raised for the bigger room.
changelog.2.0.0: Agents scale from agents.max (10): desks 1..max from a desk grid, owner colours moved from owner_1..6 / owner_N_fabric materials to one owner_colors texture used by owner_glow + owner_fabric. Overflow standing spots poi-stand-<zone>-<n>; agent-state slots fill in order and every state holds agents.max. Approach points + walk grid in scene extras. Charge bays 3 -> 4. Office Ambient clip (anim-* nodes) and baked AO (COLOR_0). Robot: bubble_q / bubble_alert joints, clips Stand, Plug_In, Plug_Out, Sit_Wait, Wait; transitions table.

world.characterForward: +Z at rest; POI rotation 0 faces +Z and is a pure yaw
world.cameraNote: overhead camera looks from +X/+Z; north (z min) and west (x min) walls are full height, south/east walls are low cutaways

loading.note: Files are meshopt-compressed with quantized attributes: the loader needs a meshopt decoder (three.js: loader.setMeshoptDecoder(MeshoptDecoder) from three/addons/libs/meshopt_decoder.module.js; Babylon.js and Unity glTFast also support it) and EXT_texture_webp. Serve with gzip or brotli: meshopt output is built to be entropy-coded by the transport (~3x smaller again). Uncompressed equivalents are built in dist/raw/ for loaders without meshopt.
loading.whyThisFormat: meshopt over Draco: it also compresses animation and morph targets (most of the robot's bytes), decodes much faster, and its decoder is a small JS/WASM file. WebP over KTX2/Basis: every texture here is small (largest 1024 px), so GPU memory is not the bottleneck and lossless WebP keeps the palette/owner lookups exact.

agents.note: Office capacity. Desks 1..max and charging bays 1..max exist, status_colors has a texel per desk, and every agent state can hold max agents at once (overflow standing spots included). To change it: set agents.max in packages/office-assets/src/office/office-layout.json (desk_grid emits the desks), update this value, rebuild. If the desk grid doesn't fit, the build says so.

poses.note: Every clip and POI kind is seated or standing. An agent state may only pair a POI with a clip of the same pose.

transitions.note: How a robot gets into and out of a POI. Walk (looping) along the walk grid to the POI's approach point, turn to the POI's yaw (rotate the root while crossfading Walk -> Idle, ~0.2 s), then play `enter` clips in order while moving the root from the approach point to the POI over the first clip; the state clip loops after that. Leaving plays `exit` in order (root back to the approach point over the last clip), then Walk. Crossfade ~0.15-0.25 s between clips. POIs with no entry here need no transition.

robot.glb.hiddenAtRestNote: props resting at scale 0. Clip-driven: zzz + cable: Charge/Plug_*, bubble_q '?': Sit_Wait/Wait, bubble_alert '!': Sit_Sad, hammer: Hammer (which also turns it about the grip). Product-driven (no clip touches them): icon_* = what a working agent is doing right now; scale the current tool's joint to 1 and the others to 0 (icon_terminal: shell commands, icon_search: reading / searching code or docs, icon_edit: changing files, icon_web: fetching / browsing). The icons sit above-left of the head (bubbles above-right), so a tool and a bubble can show together; both are fixed to the head, billboard the joint if wanted.

morphTargets.note: order is fixed; names are also in the mesh extras targetNames (three.js morphTargetDictionary)

robot.glb.materialsNote: primary is neutral grey by default: the product sets it per agent to the agent's status colour (clone material primary per agent, see statusColors). accent and eye are emissive

robot-lite.glb.materialsNote: subset of robot.glb's materials (no separate 'screen'), so the same per-agent recolouring applies
robot-lite.glb.animationsNote: ships no clips: play robot.glb's clips on it. Every robot.glb animation channel targets a node name that exists here.

minibot.glb.nodesNote: minibot = the floor point under the bot: the product sets its position and yaw (faces +Z at rest). body (its child, the mesh) hovers ~1.3 m up (above its parent's shoulder) and is animated by the clips; don't move it yourself.
minibot.glb.materialsNote: the robot's material names: clone primary per minibot and give it its parent agent's status colour (it's working for that agent). accent and eye are emissive.
minibot.glb.clipsNote: loops: Hover (idle beside its parent), Fly (moving), Work (parent working: leans in and nods). One-shots: Pop_In (spawn: scale 0 -> 1 with a little overshoot), Pop_Out (dismiss: ends at scale 0, then remove it). Every clip keys body translation, rotation and scale, so crossfades never leave it half-scaled.
minibot.glb.subAgentsNote: one minibot per running sub-agent of an agent (Claude Code Task / sub-agents), shown while it runs. Intended behaviour (office-sim has no minibot yet): it follows its parent's own path (a breadcrumb trail, so it goes round walls the parent went round) and hovers at a spot beside the parent once the parent has settled (MINIBOT_SPOTS, up to 3; show any beyond that as a count). It flies, so it doesn't use the walk grid or hold POIs.

nodePrefixes.static-: merged static geometry, one node per zone (static-<zone>); static-glass is transparent (no shadows), static-screens are emissive monitor faces. Opaque static geometry carries baked ambient occlusion in COLOR_0 (multiply into base colour; three.js does this automatically)
nodePrefixes.night-light-: KHR_lights_punctual point light; enable at night only
nodePrefixes.anim-: animated by the office clip Ambient (coolant vapour at the maintenance bar, conveyor cargo, factory arms anim-arm-N, rack shuttles anim-shuttle-N, data link anim-link): play it looping

office.glb.navMesh: node navMesh: the walk grid as geometry (y ~0.01), hide in game. Path-find on scene extras nav instead.
office.glb.poisNote: node poi-<kind>-<id>: empty node at floor level, rotation is a pure yaw (0 faces +Z). sit_work-N is work pod N (2 rows of 5 facing west) and charge-N is charging bay N (server room, west), both agent N's. sit_idle 1, 2, 5, 6 meeting-room console seats (glass room, north-west), 3-4 training pods (north-east), 7-8 lobby hang-out seats by the door; use_coffee (maintenance bar dispenser), coffee_chat (service counter); ship 1..8 = deploy workbenches (odd: Hammer, even: Tinker in the default agentStates). idle-spawn 1..5 inside the east door; idle-area-entry is the open floor inside the door. stand-<zone>-1..k are generated overflow standing spots (k depends on the layout; agent states reference them as poi-stand-<zone>-*). Every POI has an approach point (scene extras approach) on the walk grid, reachable from poi-idle-spawn-1; desk and charging seats are entered from the side or front, never through a chair back.
office.glb.materialsNote: status_glow (work pod N's front strip + floor ring, charging bay N's rack strip + header + floor ring; emissive) takes its colour from texture status_colors (scene extras statusColors): show agent N's status by writing texel N-1, e.g. swap in a W x 1 DataTexture (nearest filtering, sRGB) as status_glow's map and emissiveMap; texels with no agent use statusColors.off. lamp_glow: emissive ~off by day. palette / screens: merged flat-colour and monitor (emissive) materials, see scene extras palette / screenAtlas. agent_board: the agent board on the lobby's north wall (node agent-board, one quad); its emissive map is a baked sample: draw the live board (agents, what they're doing, where) into a canvas of agentBoard.pixels and swap it in, see agentBoard.

sceneExtrasFormats.nav: { origin: [x0, z0], cell, cols, rows, inflate, bits }: walk grid for the robot's centre (obstacles already inflated by `inflate`). bits = base64; cell (row r, col c) covers x0 + c*cell .. +cell, z0 + r*cell .. +cell; index k = r*cols + c is bit (k & 7) of byte (k >> 3), LSB first, 1 = walkable
sceneExtrasFormats.approach: { '<poi node name>': [x, z] }: where to stand before entering the POI (equal to the POI position for standing POIs on open floor)
sceneExtrasFormats.agentStates: state -> { note, color, slots: [{ pois, clip, assign? }] }; color is a statusColors key; pois are POI names, 'poi-x-*' = every POI of that kind; slots fill in order (overflow standing spots last); assign 'own' = the agent's own POI of that kind, assign 'position' = poi-<kind>-<the agent's queue position> (skipped if there is no such spot), poi-<kind>-<desk id> (its desk sit_work-N, its charging bay charge-N)
sceneExtrasFormats.statusColors: { texture: 'status_colors', width: W, desks: agents.max, materials: ['status_glow'], colors: { green, yellow, orange, red } (hex, = contract statusColors.colors), off: hex }; desk / bay N samples texel N-1 (u = (N-0.5)/W, v = 0.5)
sceneExtrasFormats.agentBoard: { node: 'agent-board', material: 'agent_board', size: [w, h] metres, pixels: [W, H] (the baked map's size, 16:9), center: [x, y, z] } ; uv (0, 0) is the board's top-left, u runs left to right, v top to bottom (three.js: texture.flipY = false, like any glTF texture)

office.glb.agentStatesNote: Every POI pattern matches at least one POI, every clip exists in robot.glb with the POI's pose, every state holds agents.max agents at once, and every state's color is a statusColors key. queued is for sessions beyond agents.max: agent slot N (pod N, bay N, status light N) belongs to one session at a time; the rest wait in the lobby queue in arrival order and the head takes the next freed slot (see Roster in packages/office-sim). The queued slot uses assign "position": a queued agent's spot is poi-stand-entry-<its queue position> (1 = nearest the door); show any beyond the last spot as a count.

statusColors.note: Colour means status, everywhere. An agent in state S shows statusColors.colors[agentStates[S].color] on its robot (clone material primary per agent and set its colour) and on its desk / charging-bay light (write texel N-1 of status_colors, see office.glb materialsNote). green = working, shipping, done; yellow = idle, paused_or_rate_limited, arrive; orange = waiting_for_input (needs the user); red = error. The office decor is deliberately muted so these stay the loudest colours in the room; keep them saturated.
